subject: some chains are much slower than others

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: some chains are much slower than others
parts:
Hi,

I am running hierarchical model which uses integrate_ode_bdf (and fastest chain runs for 24 hours). The intermediate results show (I am using stan cmd so have ability to monitor the progress) that mixing is good and pairs don't show correlations. The jacobian is supplied to speed up the process. It seems that chains should run at the same speed but they are not. I wonder why?

They were running pretty much at the same speed when I estimated the same model with one parameter fixed to nominal value. I am also using Matt's trick for random effects: N(0,sigma)=u*sigma where u~N(0,1).

Thanks for the insight,
Linas

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: some chains are much slower than others
parts:
I am using truncation which may cause slow convergence of some chains. I have used truncation to prevent non-physical values of parameters. I found that different chains converged to multiple modes (there was no switching between modes in the same chain) and so prevented chains converging to non-physical values. The stan code is attached. I am not completely sure if truncation was the right approach since the parameter is constrained to be positive and then i truncate it wit T[,1]:
theta[6] ~ lognormal(-2.94,1.3)T[,1];

Linas

> On Mar 8, 2017, at 3:17 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I am using truncation which may cause slow convergence of some chains. I have used truncation to prevent non-physical values of parameters. I found that different chains converged to multiple modes (there was no switching between modes in the same chain) and so prevented chains converging to non-physical values. The stan code is attached. I am not completely sure if truncation was the right approach since the parameter is constrained to be positive and then i truncate it wit T[,1]:
> theta[6] ~ lognormal(-2.94,1.3)T[,1];

You really want to declare theta with <lower=0, upper=1>. At which point, you don't need
the truncation statement because the parameters to the lognormal are constant.

I'm not sure what you attached because it doesn't have that truncation.

- Bob
